items.title: Jane Bunnett interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, January 25, 2024
items.q: pulling a record, “Who’s this guy Charlie Parker? Can you put this on?” And then being humiliated by the guy, “You don’t know Charlie Parker?”

ctx.x: Why didn’t you become a jazz pianist?

I had more — I had tendonitis and — yeah and I was studying classical piano and I had a very — a rebellious adolescence. I went to five high schools getting kicked out of a few of them. And I really loved art and my last year, I guess it was in an art school and I thought I wanted to paint. And I always thought I want to do this, I want to do that. And I finally got serious about piano and I went at it a little too vigorously and I developed tendonitis and then I had to take time off from the piano. I did finally…

wanted to play jazz. And I bought a flute around that time and started kind of like tinkering around on the flute. And then friends from school just on the weekends somebody would be playing, you know a couple of guitars and a bass player and we’d just be jamming on two chord things. And I don’t know what we were playing. But anyway and I would play the flute too but I really didn’t know what I was doing, but having a great time doing it. And so then I just sort of transitioned then. I started to put the things…
